narrative.overview: Weekend Tree Surgeon is a marketing site for a solo tree surgeon in Cheshire. Every pixel should feel like a recommendation from a neighbor, not a corporate pitch. The system uses warm, grounded colors pulled directly from the local landscape — golden gorse, dark plough soil, moss green — to root the brand in place. Typography pairs a friendly, high-contrast sans-serif workhorse (Roboto) with a warm, slightly retro display face (Shrikhand) that signals personality without pretension. The system is flat and print-like. Surfaces don't float; they sit. Depth is conveyed through color contrast and firm borders, not through ambient shadows. This is not a SaaS dashboard. It is not a luxury portfolio. It is a trustworthy hand extended across a garden gate.
keyCharacteristics: Warm, earthy palette drawn from Cheshire farmland
Flat surfaces with depth conveyed through color contrast, not shadows
High-contrast typography with a display face that has warmth and character
Tactile, confident buttons that reward interaction with bold state changes
Light mode as the default experience

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Gorse Gold is the only accent color on the page. It carries the brand identity on ≤15% of the visible surface. Its rarity is the point — when you see it, you know something matters.

rules.name: The No Glass Rule
rules.body: Backgrounds are opaque. No backdrop-filter, no blur(), no translucent overlays in brand sections. The mobile nav overlay is the sole exception and uses it only as a scrim.

rules.name: The Single Display Rule
rules.body: Shrikhand appears in exactly one place per page: the main headline. Nowhere else. Its impact depends on scarcity.

rules.name: The Pixel Restraint Rule
rules.body: Press Start 2P is used for the wordmark only — the three letters 'WTS' and the full business name in the footer. It is never used for headlines, body copy, labels, or navigation. Pixel fonts elsewhere read as retro-tech gimmickry.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. If an element needs to feel lifted, use color contrast or a 1px border. Shadows are prohibited.

dos: Use Gorse Gold as the sole accent — on buttons, toppers, underlines, and the services top border. Let it breathe.
Use flat surfaces with color contrast for separation. A darker background behind a lighter card is depth enough.
Use real project photos — Adam in a tree, hedges being cut, gardens being cleared. Real work, real person.
Use generous body text (1.2rem, line-height 1.5) with line lengths capped at 65-75 characters.
Use Roboto weights 400, 700, and 900 to build clear hierarchy through weight contrast alone when possible.
Respect the Single Display Rule: Shrikhand once per page.
Respect the Pixel Restraint Rule: Press Start 2P for the 'WTS' wordmark and full business name only.
Use dark mode behind a user-controlled toggle. It is never the default experience.
donts: Use box-shadow on cards, buttons, or surfaces. The Flat-By-Default Rule prohibits it.
Use the Industrial Logger aesthetic: no buzzsaws, no black/orange warning colors, no heavy machinery graphics.
Use the Cowboy Lopper look: no photos of workers without PPE, no messy job sites, no loose truck loads.
Use the Silicon Valley Tech look: no neon gradients, no glassmorphism, no dark mode as default, no sharp abstract shapes, no robotic corporate language.
Use the Elite Architect look: no ultra-minimalist white space, no high-end luxury garden layouts, no aspirational pricing cues.
Use the generic tradesman template: no stock photos of guys in hard hats, no corporate trust badges, no blue-and-white sanitized layouts.
Use border-left or border-right greater than 1px as a colored accent stripe on cards, list items, or review blocks.
Use gradient text (background-clip: text combined with any gradient background).
Round button corners. Buttons are square.
Use identical card grids with icon + heading + text repeated three times.
Treat light mode as secondary. The brand lives in light mode; dark mode is an accessibility accommodation.
